newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ING sells stake in Australia's Grand Hotel.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ING sells stake in Australia's Grand Hotel.

text.p: McIntosh Corporate Ltd said on Thursday it had concluded negotiations for the sale by ING Barings of its holding of about 39 percent of Grand Hotel Group Ltd to Singapore's Tuan Sing Holdings Ltd.
McIntosh said the purchase price of A$2.05 per share represented a total purchase price of about A$80.7 million.
"Tuan Sing has also obtained an option to purchase the holding company of the Grand Hotel Trust manager," it said.
It said the purchase was subject to the approval of GHG's non associated shareholders at a meeting expected to be held in March following an assessement by independent experts.

"Subject to the shareholder approval, the sale will extinguish any liability by McIntosh Securities Ltd under the indemnity it has granted to ING Barings in respect of its holding of securities in GHG," McIntosh said.
Grand Hotel, listed on August 12, operates the Grand Hyatt hotel in Melbourne and the Hyatt Regency in Perth.
The company's float was poorly received by investors and it has said it does not expect to meet prospectus forecasts.
ING Barings, then the largest shareholder in McIntosh with a 20 percent stake, and McIntosh itself were forced to take up just under half the stock after underwriting the issue.
McIntosh is now part of the Merrill Lynch Inc group after a takeover offer late last year.
GHG shares, offered at A$2.00 each, closed at A$1.79 on Thursday.
